article.title: With days to go before the midterms, data shows the U.S. economy is doing well
article.summary:
With days to go before the midterms, data shows the U.S. economy is doing welltoggle caption i Joe Raedle/Getty Images North AmericaThe U.S. economy grew faster in the summer compared to the spring, driven by consumer spending as well as investments in AI.
The previous quarter GDP grew at a 2.2% annual pace.
A big driver for GDP growth in the third quarter was the strong investments from AI companies, which continue to build out data centers and spend big money in developing the technology.
Meanwhile, consumer spending was another of the big drivers of GDP growth, led in part by higher-income Americans who are better able to withstand stubbornly high inflation.
Although consumer spending has been growing steadily, it has not spread out evenly across households, with lower-income Americans struggling more than high-earners.

article.title: US economy grew more than expected in 3rd quarter, government data shows
article.summary:
US economy grew more than expected in 3rd quarter, government data showsThe United States economy grew over the three months ending in September, according to a government report released on Thursday, which marked the final snapshot of the economy before next Tuesday's midterm elections.
Growth in the third quarter amounted to an acceleration from 2.2% annualized GDP growth in the previous quarter, as seen in Commerce Department data.
The performance in the third quarter also outpaced a 2.5% annualized rate recorded over the first three months of this year.
The central bank raised interest rates a quarter of a percentage point last month in an effort to battle back price woes.
Prices increased 3.7% in September compared to a year earlier, putting the inflation rate more than a percentage point above the Fed's target level of 2%, government data showed.

article.title: Polymarket Halted International Trading After Hackers Drained Accounts
article.summary:
Trading has resumed on Polymarket’s flagship international platform after a hack that drained money from the wallets of some traders.
Polymarket declined to comment when WIRED asked how many traders were impacted by the breach and how much money was lost, but the company said it will refund impacted traders.
The hack did not impact users on Polymarket US, the company’s newer platform for people within the United States.
This is not the first time that Polymarket traders have experienced security woes.
In June 2026, Polymarket experienced another breach, which resulted in over $2 million in losses for impacted traders.

On the heels of the recent rollouts of Meta’s Muse and Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon, Mistral AI is launching its new flagship frontier model, Mistral Large 4.

article.title: What the Fed's interest rate decision means for your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
article.summary:
The national average interest rate on checking accounts has barely budged this year, remaining at 0.07%.
This is one category where rate shopping and subsequent increases in the Fed rate really pay off.
The federal funds rate doesn't directly determine federal student loan interest rates, but it can influence them indirectly.
Congress sets the federal student loan rates based on the 10-year Treasury note, adding a fixed margin each year.
When investors expect high inflation or strong economic growth, they demand higher yields, which can push federal student loan rates higher.

article.title: Syrians grow frustrated as soaring living costs threaten recovery
article.summary:
People burned tyres, blocked roads and chanted slogans, angry at the government's decision to raise fuel prices again.
It was the largest show of discontent yet since President Ahmed al-Sharaa came to power two years ago.
But as they celebrated Assad's overthrow and their new freedoms, Syrians, perhaps unrealistically, hoped things would quickly improve.
And many saw a further and unexpected rise in fuel prices as a sign of a government out of touch with its country.
People stood by you and are still with you," another protester said, addressing Sharaa, "but this will [make] things explode".

article.title: Europe's youth are protesting - and feeling locked out of a future
article.summary:
From Milan, to Marseille, to Madrid and in so many other cities across Europe, streets have erupted in colourful, passionate protests in recent weeks.
While most started peacefully, a large number ended in shocking scenes of violence and looting.
In Lisbon, tens of thousands of mostly young people marched earlier this month.
In Albania, demonstrators alleging government corruption are demanding that their Prime Minister Edi Rama - already 13 years in power - stand down.
I've spent years in Europe reporting from a multitude of demonstrations, both peaceful and violent.

The main themes of the two-day state visit to Guyana will be the environment and sustainability - alongside the growing commercial ties between the UK and Guyana.
Guyana - formerly British Guiana - is the world's fastest growing economy due to the discovery of oil reserves there in 2015.
As the King left the Bahamas on Thursday to fly to Guyana, his spokesman said the islands he was departing had "a special place in the King's heart".

article.title: Alphabet Is in Talks to Join Trump’s Golden Dome Defense Program
article.summary:
(Bloomberg) -- Alphabet Inc.'s Google is in talks with the US Defense Department to work on a new data security effort underpinning the $185 billion Golden Dome missile defense program, according to people familiar with the matter.
The talks have focused on Google's data storage, networking and cybersecurity capabilities, one of the people said.
Golden Dome is President Donald Trump's marquee defense program to build a layer of defense systems from ground to space that will protect the US from foreign attack.
The effort would mark Google's first publicly known involvement in the Golden Dome program and another sign of how the search engine giant is continuing to lean into national security and defense work.
Both the Pentagon's separate Golden Dome initiatives to pioneer space-based missile interceptors and its command-and-control consortium rely on numerous companies from startups to established primes, unlike past defense programs that have been more typically anchored by a single, large contractor.

article.title: Apple’s new laptop supports one of the coolest features for color pros
article.summary:
It’s the first laptop, and only the second product overall, to support Apple CMF 2026 color modes.
The specification that’s been the standard for years is CIE 1931 (CIE stands for Commission Internationale de l’Éclairage, or International Commission on Illumination).
CIE 1931 doesn’t properly handle that and was created based on only 17 test subjects.
Apple CMF 2026 addresses that, so that displays look the same regardless of the technology they use.
Color science and display technologies have come a long way since 1931, when the CIE 1931 color space was established.

article.title: South West Water given lowest environmental rating
article.summary:
South West Water has been given the lowest possible environmental rating by the Environment Agency over high levels of pollution.
The regulator downgraded the firm from two stars out of a possible four to one, meaning it is now considered a "poor performing company" for its environmental impact.
South West Water, which has 1.8 million customers across Devon, Cornwall, the Isles of Scilly and parts of Dorset and Somerset, said it knew there was "much more to do" and was taking action to improve areas that "matter most" to customers and the environment.
The annual Environmental Performance Assessment grades England's nine water and sewerage companies largely on how often they pollute rivers, streams and the sea.
For 2025, South West Water was among four companies rated as poor performing, or one star, while four others were rated as requiring improvement, two stars.

article.title: Google’s latest Nest Learning Thermostat is $60 off just in time for sweater weather
article.summary:
As the weather cools, it may be worth investing in a smart thermostat to help lower your energy bills.
Right now, Google’s fourth-gen Nest Learning Thermostat is on sale in all three colors for $219.99 ($60 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and The Home Depot, matching its best price of the year and just $10 shy of its all-time low.
Google’s latest Nest Learning Thermostat is its most capable to date, and comes with new features designed to lower energy consumption without sacrificing comfort.
It can also suggest schedule changes to save energy and automatically adjusts the temperature when you’re away.
The Nest Learning Thermostat also improves on its predecessor with a beautifully designed adaptive display that shows your temperature settings, the weather, and the time from across the room.

article.title: Montana acquires sustainable furniture maker Takt
article.summary:
Montana has announced its buyout of fellow Danish design brand Takt, known for its solid wood furniture and pioneering approach to sustainable design.
Founded in 2019 by trained physicist and former Lego and Bang & Olufsen executive Henrik Taudorf Lorensen, Takt makes modern Scandinavian furniture from FSC-certified wood that is low-carbon, flat-pack and designed for disassembly.
“Takt brings experience with materials and the environment, and we are looking forward to bringing our respective experience together and taking this work even further,” he said.
By gaining access to the established, international infrastructure of Montana, which has been operating since 1982, Lorensen hopes that Takt’s furniture will be able to reach a larger audience.
““Now it is time for TAKT’s next chapter, and we are delighted that it will be written together with Montana.”

article.title: Rivian’s R2 is officially its best-selling vehicle
article.summary:
Rivian made $176 million in gross profit this quarter, a $152 million improvement compared to the same time last year.
Rivian is losing less than it did a year ago because they sold more cars and made more money per vehicle.
Earlier this month, Rivian reported a record sales quarter, with 19,751 vehicles produced and 19,248 delivered.
But the company said that the R2 is now the “best-selling Rivian vehicle by volume,” outselling the R1T and R1S, as well as the Electric Delivery Van (EDV).
“We had great results with R2 becoming our best selling vehicle by volume in the third quarter,” Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe said in a statement, ahead of the company’s earnings call this afternoon.

article.title: UK weather: 10 days without rain after 'wettest week in two years'
article.summary:
The UK could see as many as 10 consecutive days without rain after an unsettled end to October that featured back-to-back storms.
It comes after the Environment Agency said England experienced its wettest week in two years thanks to Storms Austen and Boelo.
Following this recent unsettled weather, the return of high pressure will bring a prolonged spell of largely dry and calm conditions, with very little rain in sight.
Mist and fog will remain a persistent feature, with some slow-clearing dense patches expected during the mornings.

article.title: Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk
article.summary:
“A lot of people want local inference.
And somehow, they assume that the problem is solved now because we are going to have open-source models, we’re going to be able to run them on our computers, and so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center.
But from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used five percent of the time.

article.title: RAF base chemical contamination worst in UK, report finds
article.summary:
Chemical contamination at a former RAF base earmarked for 9,000 homes is the worst found in the UK, a report has said.
Testing at RAF Upper Heyford carried out on behalf of a developer found "unacceptable" levels of polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), referred to as forever chemicals.
At RAF Upper Heyford, firefighters would practice putting out an aeroplane set on fire above a "pond" of fuel.
This training area was found to be "the most significant ongoing source of PFAS contamination identified" - a few hundred metres north of existing developments.
Another report into ground and surface water found contamination was "widespread" at the site, with all samples exceeding environmental standards.

article.title: Global nature talks reach deal but money remains an issue
article.summary:
The world's nations have been gathered in Yerevan for nearly two weeks negotiating, and arguing, over a new agreement on nature.
Early on Saturday morning, hours after talks were due to finish, they finally agreed the key parts of a new action plan.
Four years earlier the same countries had signed a landmark deal committing to "halt and reverse" the decline of nature.
That global deal in 2022 - the Global Biodiversity Framework - contained 24 targets including putting 30% of the world's land and seas into protection by the end of the decade.
As part of this week's deal, countries acknowledged they were falling behind.

article.title: Battery Prototype Uses Superextensive Quantum Effects To Charge Faster
article.summary:

demonstrate in a recent paper does seem to suggest that it uses quantum effects to charge faster than would otherwise be possible, with this rate increasing faster than its volume, meaning at a superextensive rate.
The general idea behind a quantum battery is that these somehow use a quantum effect to store and release energy faster than would be possible using classical physics.
First proposed in 2013, the initial Dicke model saw its theoretical quantum advantage shot down by 2020, leading to the search for alternative models.
Effectively scaling up the cell would thus scale up the charge- and discharge rate faster than in a conventional chemical cell.
